prompt:
Scene:
A square cinematic matte-painting style illustration of an imagined 21st-century spaceport as envisioned in 1956, wide establishing shot, camera slightly low three-quarter angle. Powder-blue daytime sky with a few wispy clouds. Warm afternoon sun gives long cinematic shadows across the concrete launch apron. Subtle film-grain texture and the gentle color grading of a vintage Cinerama travel short.

Subject:
In center-frame a massive silver finned passenger rocket stands upright on a polished concrete pad, held by a spiral latticework gantry. Its body is polished chrome with three horizontal cadmium-red stripes and a large cockpit porthole halfway up. To the left rises an art-deco spire terminal building in ivory stone with chrome fluting, crowned by a glass observation dome ringed with bright yellow neon piping. A curving pedestrian skybridge connects the spire to the gantry. Small stylized figures in pastel flight suits and bubble helmets wait in a neat line at the base. Parked chrome-finned family ground-cars sit beyond a yellow railing. A small control tower with a rotating beacon stands off to the right.

Important details:
Strict atomic-age palette: ivory, turquoise, cadmium red, bright yellow, powder pink, chrome, powder blue sky. Rocket body must read as an exaggerated 1959-Cadillac-fin-style passenger ship, not a modern spacecraft. Terminal must read as art-deco meets Googie: fluted spire, curving canopies, neon trim, ornamental finials. Keep painted-matte-painting feel, slight brush texture, soft atmospheric haze toward the horizon. People are stylized figures, not photoreal.

Use case:
Root reference image for the Silver Rocket Terminal series. Later images will reuse this rocket and terminal silhouette.

Constraints:
No readable text, no watermark, no logos, no modern SpaceX-style rockets, no photorealistic crowd, no drab industrial steel, no glass-box minimalist architecture, no smartphones, preserve exact 1:1 aspect ratio.
